findings: As WP-27g's F1/F3: the statement involves \widetilde M (resp. lem:dense_orbits, spread_connected_image), which need the base locally path-connected (prop:universality, §3 standing l.810); a singular (G,X)-manifold is only locally connected (l.474), so 'locally path-connected' is carried.

l.1811–1819, the proof uses \widehat M = \widetilde M^{S ∪ sing M}, which exists only when M ∖ (S ∪ sing M) is semilocally simply connected; this is supplied by the section's standing assumption X locally unloopable (l.1660, via lem:analytical_structure_locally_unloopable) — the dependence is made explicit in GX.singular_developing_theorem_of_slsc.

l.1812–1819: the formal proof does not use \widehat M' nor lem:descend_developing_map; it compares D ∘ Φ (Φ : \widehat M → N) and F ∘ Ψ (Ψ : \widehat M → \widetilde M, F the classical developing map of the simply connected \widetilde{reg M}) on the connected \widehat M ∖ \widehat S (they differ by one g), and descends D ∘ Φ along the open map Ψ (constancy on fibres by density of \widetilde M ∖ \widetilde S and openness of Ψ). The paper's 'Γ(\widehat M'/\widetilde reg(M)) = Γ(\widehat M/\widetilde M)' and 'the action of Γ on \widehat D_0 is trivial … apply lem:descend again' are thus not needed.
questions: prop:branched_devmap (l.1807): accept 'M locally path-connected' (the hypothesis of prop:universality under which \widetilde M is defined, as WP-27g F1/F3)? Under it the row closes (GX.singular_developing_theorem, with X locally unloopable as the section's standing hypothesis).

kb_proposals: A developing map on a simply connected cover inside a singular manifold: GX.exists_developing_of_simplyConnected turns GX.exists_developingMap into the a.e. language (a local homeomorphism π : Z → supp B; chartedSpaceOfAtlas on π^*B, whose support is univ by mem_support_of_isLocalHomeomorphOn').

To descend a map along a branched covering Ψ: prove constancy on fibres over a dense open set, then on all fibres by T2 separation + Ψ open (spread_connected_image) + density; continuity by IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap. No deck transformations are needed.
`set S := Sing G X M` in a proof whose statement has `y₀ : (Sing G X M)ᶜ` duplicates y₀ (y₀✝) and the final `exact` fails; write the set out instead.
